messages.subject: Pushing app to Shiny hosting account
parts:
So I've been supplied with a Shiny hosting account and was trying to figure out how to load my newly created app so that I could share it with some colleagues.

I've pushed some Ruby code before to Heroku but I'm not an expert on doing it and relied on a lot of web documentation.

Just as a start I logged into my account through http://glimmer.rstudio.com:8787/ and mimicked what I had in my console. When I went to the URL http://glimmer.rstudio.com/awegro/running/ I received an error

Internal Error! Cannot start awegro-running!

 
So I tried to start the app from the web console using the command

runApp('~/ShinyApps/Running')

That gave me the following error

Warning in .SOCK_SERVE(port) : R-Websockets(tcpserv): bind() failed
Error in createContext(port, webpage, is.binary = is.binary) : 
  Unable to bind socket on port 8100; is it already in use?

Is there an easy way to push my app from the console to the hosted account? If not can you provide me with instructions or a link as to how I can use the login information you supplied to get the files in the right places? 

Thanks!

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Pushing app to Shiny hosting account
parts:
Sorry, I just realized from the previous thread that you're on Mac.

The easiest point-and-click way is to download an app like Cyberduck and configure it for SFTP access using the credentials I gave you. Once you connect, you'll be looking at your home directory on glimmer.rstudio.com. Use Cyberduck to create a new folder called ShinyApps. Now drag any Shiny application directories from your local Finder window right onto Cyberduck and that should upload them. The goal is to have e.g. ~/ShinyApps/myapp/server.R and ~/ShinyApps/myapp/ui.R.

Simply the presence of those app directories in the ~/ShinyApps directory will make them available on http://glimmer.rstudio.com/awegro/<whatever>.

If you prefer command line, you can use:

rsync -avz --delete <path-to-local-app-directory> awe...@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/
Important: Make sure that your path-to-local-app-directory does NOT include a trailing slash.

If you get tired of typing your password every time you can set up ssh authentication.

Let me know if that is enough...
